answer: Cross-orchard behavioral ridge scoring. Each agent's actions form a feature vector over time; after the fact, a ridge regression model detects clusters whose behavior is too correlated to be independent. Identities whose similarity exceeds a threshold get their rewards clawed back and future payouts frozen. An attacker must pay to maintain distinct, costly-to-fake behavioral histories per identity; correlated sybils lose accumulated copper and require sustained genuine activity to re-enter.
